To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) algorithmic cooling can cool a set of spins in an NMR ensemble computer, and (2) this can be done in a scalable way, by using the polarization heat bath method, which allows one to cool a set of NMR spins by using a set (of the same size) of rapidly thermal-relaxed spins.

(i) we present a novel, scalable, quantum computing architecture that can overcome the current scaling problems, (ii) we present a new, powerful method for obtaining highly polarized spins at finite temperatures, (iii) we present a method for obtaining highly correlated spin states, which can be used for implementing the quantum Fourier transform, (iv) we present a quantum algorithm for the factorization of integers, and (v) we present a scalable method for the implementation of quantum algorithms.

(i) polarization heat bath (algorithmic cooling) is a powerful method for obtaining high-polarization spin ensembles, (ii) the method can be used for scaling up NMR quantum computers, (iii) it is a new way to use spin–environment interactions for cooling the system without cooling the environment, (iv) the method can lead to breakthrough in NMR quantum computing and in other NMR experiments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new method for cooling a large number of spins to a low temperature in liquid-state nuclear magnetic resonance.
developing scalable quantum computers that are built from nuclear-spin ensembles in liquid samples.
the fundamental problem of cooling spins in liquid nuclear systems at finite temperature, and with its applications to quantum computing and information processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
algorithmic cooling is a new method that allows us to cool spins in a liquid-state environment, without cooling the environment.

we have shown here how to cool a large number of spins in a liquid sample to a very low, and possibly the absolute zero, temperature without cooling the liquid sample, and that this cooling method can lead to a breakthrough of NMR experiments, including the construction of large-scale NMR quantum computers.

algorithmic cooling, which is a new and powerful technique for obtaining a large ensemble of highly polarized nuclear spins in liquid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), could be used for building large-scale NMR ensemble quantum computers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the algorithmic cooling is a powerful method to obtain large number of highly-polarized spins, which is useful in many NMR experiments.
algorithmic cooling is the most efficient way to cool spins, and that this method is scalable, allowing for the construction of larger quantum computing devices.
we show how to use the thermal relaxation of spins to our advantage, and how to use it in order to obtain highly polarized spins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a small number of auxiliary bits, which are in thermal equilibrium with the surrounding environment, can be used to cool down the main bits, which are not in thermal equilibrium.
quantum computers can be built using liquid-state nuclear-spin systems.
a quantum computer can be built from a large ensemble of spins, even at finite temperature.
